methodology.title: Security reasoning connected to the system.
methodology.subtitle: From protected assets to verifiable requirements and assurance evidence.
introduction: System Security-Theoretic Process Analysis is a human- and asset-centered approach to engineering secure complex systems. It connects the architecture and operating context to the assets that matter, the ways their protection could fail, and the evidence needed to judge the security solution.

SSTPA Tools implements this approach as a shared graph model. Specialized tools operate on a selected System of Interest, so architecture, states, exposure, attacks, requirements, and assurance arguments remain related as the design develops.

differentiator.title: A specific protection objective anchors the analysis.
differentiator.body: SSTPA defines a loss as the compromise of a security attribute on an asset. Loss analysis is scoped to an operating environment and the applicable regime. This combination of asset, property, environment, and authority gives security reasoning a concrete subject and makes its assumptions available for review.

principles.title: Assets establish the protection objective
principles.body: Begin with items of value whose compromise could harm stakeholders. Keep the asset distinct from the component that hosts it, and record the security attributes and regimes that govern its protection.

principles.title: Interactions and states expose the problem
principles.body: Analyze behavior, control, feedback, and asset exposure across architecture and operating states. A component-level view alone cannot describe every interaction that matters.

principles.title: Requirements make the response implementable
principles.body: Translate controls and countermeasures into system security requirements. Allocate them to the design and define how their implementation will be verified.

principles.title: Evidence supports human judgment
principles.body: Use loss analysis and GSN arguments to show what supports the security claim, which assumptions apply, and what remains unresolved. The responsible authority decides whether residual risk is acceptable.

protectionAttributes.name: Confidentiality
protectionAttributes.description: Access is restricted to authorized parties.

protectionAttributes.name: Integrity
protectionAttributes.description: The asset is protected against unauthorized modification or destruction.

protectionAttributes.name: Availability
protectionAttributes.description: Authorized users can obtain the asset or service when needed.

protectionAttributes.name: Authenticity
protectionAttributes.description: The asset or claimed identity is genuine and can be verified.

protectionAttributes.name: Non-Repudiation
protectionAttributes.description: Evidence of origin or occurrence can be established under stated assumptions.

protectionAttributes.name: Privacy
protectionAttributes.description: Risks to individuals are managed against applicable privacy objectives.

protectionAttributes.name: Trustworthiness
protectionAttributes.description: There is justified confidence in the required behavior.

protectionAttributes.name: Certifiability
protectionAttributes.description: SSTPA’s protection objective for achieving and maintaining certification within a regime.

workflow.title: Establish the Tier-1 architecture
workflow.description: Capture the capability requirements, Tier-1 systems, and connections from the program’s functional architecture.
workflow.output: Allocated capability requirements and an explicit architecture.

workflow.title: Allocate requirements and join interfaces
workflow.description: Decompose security requirements onto interfaces, functions, and components; connect the interfaces that participate in each system connection.
workflow.output: Architecture elements with requirements and interface participation.

workflow.title: Record assets and protection obligations
workflow.description: Bring expert asset-identification results into the model. Define asset parentage, criticality, required security attributes, and governing regimes.
workflow.output: A defined asset set with protection objectives.

workflow.title: Define system security states
workflow.description: Describe states with a consistent protection posture and the criteria for transitions, aligned with the program’s functional state model.
workflow.output: Security states, transitions, and environment validity.

workflow.title: Define environments and research threats
workflow.description: Describe relevant operating environments and the threats that could act within them. Research applicable reference knowledge.
workflow.output: An explicit operating context and relevant threat knowledge.

workflow.title: Analyze hazardous conditions
workflow.description: Connect hazards to their environments, states, threatened assets, and constraints.
workflow.output: Hazards grounded in the system’s actual operating conditions.

workflow.title: Analyze functional and control behavior
workflow.description: Use functional flows and STPA control structures to identify requirements for control actions, feedback, and process knowledge.
workflow.output: Security requirements and countermeasures derived from behavior.

workflow.title: Develop controls to mitigate hazards
workflow.description: Categorize the system, select and tailor a controls baseline, and connect controls to hazards and implementing requirements.
workflow.output: A tailored baseline with traceable model controls.

workflow.title: Define validation and verification criteria
workflow.description: Record how the security solution will satisfy its purpose and controls, and how implementing requirements will be verified.
workflow.output: Purpose-level validation and requirement-level verification criteria.

workflow.title: Trace asset exposure through states
workflow.description: For each asset, record the components, functions, and interfaces that hold, transport, or use it in each security state.
workflow.output: State-scoped exposure and inherited protection obligations.

workflow.title: Develop actionable attacks
workflow.description: Connect applicable attacks to exposed architecture elements. Add hierarchy, metrics, reference sources, and loss scope as needed.
workflow.output: Attacks ready to participate in loss analysis.

workflow.title: Analyze losses and remaining vulnerability
workflow.description: Build and tailor an attack tree for an asset protection objective in one environment. Examine paths, countermeasures, and residual vulnerabilities.
workflow.output: Loss analysis with documented scenario dispositions and rationale.

workflow.title: Construct and review the assurance argument
workflow.description: Build a GSN argument supported by validation, verification, and loss evidence. Record the responsible authority’s disposition and any conditions.
workflow.output: An evidence-backed argument for review, or a defined design revision.

workflow.title: Decompose and integrate child systems
workflow.description: Refine components into child Systems of Interest and repeat the analysis at each tier. Gather verification and validation evidence during integration.
workflow.output: Connected security reasoning and evidence across the hierarchy.

loops.title: Revise the design when the argument needs it
loops.body: If evidence is insufficient or the residual risk is unacceptable, return to functional and STPA analysis. Strengthen the countermeasures and requirements, then refresh controls, validation, traces, attacks, and losses before rebuilding the argument.

loops.title: Repeat the discipline at every system tier
loops.body: A component can become a child System of Interest. Requirements and asset parentage remain connected to the upper tiers, while asset traces are established again in the child. Verification and validation evidence accumulates as the systems are integrated.

methodology.workflowNote: The fourteen steps follow the current white paper. Tools support the work without enforcing its order. Use-Case supports early architecture capture, Reference research is cross-cutting, and Reports packages results throughout.

ecosystem.title: Fits into the engineering program
ecosystem.body: The program’s existing requirements, functional modeling, and analytical tools retain their respective roles. SSTPA is the working model for the System Security Solution, using architecture faithfully captured from those sources.

roles.sstpa: Align security requirement derivation and allocation with the program baseline.
Capture the functions, interfaces, components, and context needed for security analysis.
Use relevant results to inform functional and control analysis.
Connect assets, loss analysis, security controls, requirements, and assurance evidence.

assurance.title: Review the claim, the evidence, and the conditions.
assurance.body: A GSN argument structures the reasoning; it does not itself constitute acceptance. Closure is assessed within the approved asset scope, architecture baseline, environments, threat assumptions, and coverage criteria. Scenarios with unacceptable risk or insufficient evidence remain open.
assurance.arv: Allowed Residual Vulnerability is SSTPA’s term for an accepted residual vulnerability under documented conditions. The acceptance record identifies the deciding authority, configuration, regime, conditions, and review triggers.

glossary.definition: The selected system and its subgraph on which most tools operate.
An item of value requiring protection, distinct from the architecture that holds, transports, or uses it.
The property to protect. Assurance is the justified confidence that the required property holds.
The authority, rules, obligations, and practices under which the security solution and residual risk are judged.
Evidence that a specified requirement was implemented.
Evidence that the realized system fulfills its intended purpose in its intended environment.

example.name: FireSat
example.title: One mission. A connected system of systems.
example.description: A forest-fire detection and response capability spanning space, command, aviation, and ground systems. Follow the Fire Detection Payload from infrared sensing to detection reports, then build its security analysis in tutorial exercises.
example.scopeNote: FireSat is an educational architecture, not a validated operational design. Its supplied structure includes systems, states, functions, interfaces, connections, and requirements. Assets, traces, use cases, control structures, losses, countermeasures, and assurance arguments are developed in the tutorials.

installationAdmin.title: Give the engineering model a dependable home.
installationAdmin.subtitle: Prepare the environment. Establish its people and projects. Open a connected workspace.
installationAdmin.introduction: SSTPA Tools separates the installer, startup software, desktop interface, and backend into four independently operable segments. Administrators establish the environment and stewardship that let engineers work from a shared model.

steps.title: Install the release package
steps.body: Use the platform-specific install helper for Linux, macOS, or Windows. The installer checks Docker and Compose, stages the packaged components, and generates credentials for that installation.

steps.title: Establish a trusted connection
steps.body: The packaged trust helper installs the local Caddy certificate authority for the desktop interface. The installer attempts this setup when Docker is reachable; the guide covers checking and completing it.

steps.title: Start and establish RootAdmin
steps.body: Launch the Startup Software. It starts the backend, guides first-run RootAdmin creation, authenticates the session, and opens the desktop workspace.

steps.title: Load knowledge and the example
steps.body: Load the validated Reference Data package after the backend is healthy. FireSat is a separate example package with checksum verification and a guard against colliding with existing model identities.

steps.title: Establish project stewardship
steps.body: Use the authorized administrative workflows for accounts, ownership, and sandboxes. Establish the project context that engineers will use and confirm that the intended users can sign in.

steps.title: Enter the engineering workspace
steps.body: Open Navigator, choose the project, and select a System of Interest. For the FireSat walkthrough, follow Space Segment → FireSat Satellite → Fire Detection Payload.

backend.title: The services behind the workspace
backend.description: The desktop interface operates on a shared graph through the backend. Model changes are validated and committed transactionally.
